title: Untitled
content:
FastAPI Complete Notes (Video 1 → 6) + Senior-Dev Insights

Source: Pratik Mishra ki FastAPI series (Hinglish). Notes video ke flow ke hisaab se hain, filler hata diya hai. Har video ke baad 🧠 Insight section hai: wo cheezein jo log 10 saal kaam karke seekhte hain. ⚠️ Correction = video me jo cheez simplified ya galat thi, uska sahi version.

Table of Contents

  1. Video 1: Intro, FastAPI kyun?, Roadmap
  2. Video 2: Setup
  3. Video 3: First server + GET endpoint
  4. Video 4: Path Params & Query Params
  5. Video 5: HTTP Methods (theory)
  6. Video 6: POST, PUT, DELETE + Pydantic DTO
  7. Final code (jo video me bana)
  8. Production-grade version (same API, sahi tareeke se)
  9. Assumptions / Doubts solved
  10. 10-saal-wale lessons cheat sheet
  11. Aage ka roadmap

<a id="video-1"></a>

Video 1: Introduction, FastAPI kyun seekhein

FastAPI kya hai?

  • Python ka web framework hai. Python se backend / web app / API banani ho to use kar sakte ho.
  • Market me aur frameworks: Django, Flask, Django Ninja.

Video ke 5 reasons

# Reason Matlab
1 Speed Complex requests handle karne wala fast response deta hai. Microservices support bhi karta hai (app ko chhote parts me todna).
2 Pydantic pe bana hai Data validation + data parsing automatic milti hai.
3 Seekhna easy Baaki frameworks ke comparison me jaldi seekh sakte ho.
4 Async programming Ek saath multiple requests handle ho sakti hain, response bhi simultaneously.
5 Jobs Job openings zyada hain (video ka claim).

Series me kya cover hoga (roadmap)

  • CRUD operations: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE endpoints
  • Databases connect karna: PostgreSQL, MySQL (SQL databases)
  • Authentication: register → login → token generate (backend ki "jad")
  • User ko email bhejna (registration confirmation)
  • Background tasks: email bhejne jaisa slow kaam response block kiye bina background me

🧠 Insight (Video 1)

  1. "FastAPI sabse fast hai" ka sahi matlab. Python frameworks me ye top tier me hai (Starlette + uvicorn ki wajah se). Lekin real apps me bottleneck 95% database / network / external API hota hai, framework nahi. Framework ki speed se zyada important: query optimisation, indexes, caching, connection pooling.
  2. Async ka matlab "fast" nahi, "concurrent" hai. Async tab chamakta hai jab kaam I/O wait wala ho (DB, HTTP calls). CPU-heavy kaam (image processing, ML inference) async se fast nahi hoga. Uske liye process pool / Celery / alag worker service.
  3. Framework ek tool hai. Video me bola "jo bhi language ho concept same hai". Ye 100% sach hai. HTTP, REST, auth, validation, DB design: ye evergreen skills hain. Tum MERN jaante ho to Express ↔ FastAPI ka mapping seekhna sabse tez rasta hai:
Express (Node) FastAPI
app.get('/x', handler) @app.get("/x") decorator
req.params Path parameters (function args)
req.query Query parameters (function args)
req.body + Joi/Zod Pydantic model
res.status(404).json() raise HTTPException(404)
nodemon fastapi dev (auto-reload)
Swagger manually setup /docs free me milta hai
  1. Microservices ka trap. Beginner sab kuch microservices me todta hai. Seniors ka rule: pehle modular monolith, microservices tab jab team/scale ki real zarurat ho.

<a id="video-2"></a>

Video 2: FastAPI Setup

Step 1: Python aur pip check

bash
python --version
pip --version

Windows me cmd kholo, Linux/Mac me terminal. Agar error aaye to pehle Python install karo.

Step 2: Project folder

Desktop pe naya folder (e.g. fastapi-basics) banao, VS Code me open karo.

Step 3: Virtual environment

bash
python -m venv venv

Activate:

bash
# Linux / Mac
source venv/bin/activate

# Windows
.\venv\Scripts\activate

Activate hone pe terminal me (venv) dikhega.

Step 4: FastAPI install

bash
pip install "fastapi[standard]"

Ek hi command me FastAPI + zaruri modules aa jaate hain, jaise:

  • python-dotenv: .env files load karne ke liye
  • uvicorn: server jo FastAPI app ko serve karta hai (server start karta hai)

Step 5: Verify

main.py banao:

python
import fastapi
print(fastapi.__version__)
bash
python main.py

Version print ho gaya = install sahi.

🧠 Insight (Video 2)

  1. ⚠️ Correction: command me quotes lagao: pip install "fastapi[standard]". Zsh (Mac) me bina quotes ke [] ka matlab alag hota hai aur error aata hai.
  2. Virtual env kyun? Har project ki apni dependencies. Warna ek project ka package version dusre ko tod deta hai. Ye "works on my machine" problem ki pehli line of defence hai.
  3. venv/ ko kabhi git me commit mat karo. .gitignore me venv/, .env, __pycache__/ daalo.
  4. Dependencies freeze karo:
    bash
    pip freeze > requirements.txt
    Better: aaj kal uv (Astral) bahut fast hai aur pyproject.toml + lockfile deta hai. Team projects me lockfile = reproducible builds.
  5. ASGI vs WSGI: Flask/Django (purana style) WSGI hain (sync). FastAPI ASGI hai (async support). Uvicorn ek ASGI server hai. Production me aksar gunicorn -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker ya seedha uvicorn --workers N ya fastapi run.
  6. Python version pin karo (e.g. 3.11/3.12). Video me jo version bola, transcript me garbled hai, apna stable version use karo.

<a id="video-3"></a>

Video 3: Pehla server + pehla GET endpoint

Server banana (sirf 2 lines)

python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
  • FastAPI ek class hai, app uska object.
  • Bas itna likhne se "server ready" ho jaata hai (run karna baaki hai).

Server run karna

bash
fastapi dev main.py
  • python main.py nahi, kyunki hume file ko Python ki tarah run nahi, FastAPI ke through serve karni hai.
  • Output: server http://127.0.0.1:8000 pe chal raha hai.

Address ka matlab

Part Matlab
127.0.0.1 localhost: tumhara apna system. Sabke system me same.
8000 Port number: system ka "darwaza" jisse browser/devices andar aate hain. Badal bhi sakte ho.

Browser me kholo

Abhi {"detail": "Not Found"} dikhega. Iska matlab: server chal raha hai, bas koi route configure nahi kiya.

Endpoint kya hota hai?

Jab tum kisi website ka URL visit karte ho (/about), us particular URL pe server kuch data return karta hai. Wo URL + uska response decide karne wala logic = endpoint.

Pehla endpoint banana

python
@app.get("/")
def home():
    return "Welcome to FastAPI series"

Teen cheezein samjho:

  1. Normal function banao (home).
  2. Decorator @app.get("/") lagao. Ye FastAPI ko batata hai ki "ye function normal nahi, ek route/endpoint hai".
  3. get = HTTP method. "/" = path (default home route).

Path ke rules

  • "/" ka matlab: 8000 ke baad koi extra path nahi.
  • "/home" likhoge to URL hoga http://127.0.0.1:8000/home (tabhi chalega jab ye URL visit karo).
  • Doosra endpoint:
    python
    @app.get("/connect")def contact():    return "You can connect us anytime"
  • Same route kabhi repeat nahi hota (same method + same path). Warna system confuse ho jaata hai ki kaunsa function call karna hai.
  • Ek project me n number of routes ho sakte hain.

🧠 Insight (Video 3)

  1. /docs ek bar zaroor kholo: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs (Swagger UI) aur /redoc. FastAPI tumhare code se OpenAPI schema auto-generate karta hai. Yahin se tum bina Postman ke bhi POST/PUT/DELETE test kar sakte ho. Ye Express me manually karna padta hai.
  2. fastapi dev vs fastapi run: dev = auto-reload ON, debug friendly (sirf development). run = production mode. Production me reload kabhi on mat rakho.
  3. Decorator = registration. @app.get("/") internally route ko router table me register karta hai. Isi liye same method+path duplicate nahi chalta (pehla match jeetta hai, doosra silently dead code ban jaata hai: ye bug dhundhna mushkil hota hai).
  4. {"detail": "Not Found"} = 404. Ye sahi behaviour hai. Server up hai, route nahi mila.
  5. Route order matters. FastAPI routes ko upar se neeche match karta hai. Example:
    python
    @app.get("/products/{product_id}")   # pehle ye@app.get("/products/featured")       # ye kabhi hit nahi hoga: "featured" ko product_id maan lega
    Fix: static routes (/products/featured) ko dynamic routes (/products/{id}) se pehle define karo.
  6. def vs async def: Plain def handler FastAPI ek threadpool me chalata hai (blocking safe). async def handler event loop pe chalta hai, agar usme blocking call (jaise time.sleep(), requests.get(), sync DB driver) kar di to poora server freeze ho jaata hai. Rule:
    • Async library use kar rahe ho (httpx, asyncpg, motor) → async def
    • Sync library (requests, psycopg2, normal SQLAlchemy sync) → plain def Ye FastAPI ki sabse common production galti hai.
  7. Return type: string, dict, list, Pydantic model: sab JSON me convert ho jaate hain. Real APIs me hamesha dict/object return karo, bare string nahi (extensible rehta hai).

<a id="video-4"></a>

Video 4: Path Parameters & Query Parameters

Setup: Mock data

contact route hata ke products router banaya jo products ki list deta hai. Database abhi nahi hai to mock data (hard-coded data, jo real DB se nahi aa raha).

mock_data.py:

python
products = [
    {"id": 1, "title": "mobile phone", "price": 1000, "count": 10},
    {"id": 2, "title": "Apple MacBook", "price": 10000, "count": 12},
]

main.py:

python
from mock_data import products

@app.get("/products")
def get_products():
    return products

Browser me /products → saare products. (Jaise Amazon/Flipkart ka listing page.)

Sirf function likhna kaafi nahi, @app.get(...) decorator na lagao to wo route nahi banta. Video me ye bhool gaye the aur "Not Found" aaya.

Problem

Mujhe ek specific product chahiye (id=1, id=2...). To frontend se backend ko id pass karni padegi (URL ke through, GET me). Do tareeke:

Tareeka 1: Path Parameter

Endpoint ke baad / laga ke dynamic value:

/product/1      /product/10      /product/100

Backend ke liye dynamic, frontend ke liye ek fixed value.

Real-life example: Gmail me mail.google.com/mail/u/0 → 0 ko 1 karo to doosra account khulta hai. Ye number dynamic hai = path param.

Code:

python
@app.get("/product/{product_id}")
def get_one_product(product_id: int):
    return {"id": product_id}
  • {product_id} curly braces = "yahan dynamic value aayegi" (jaise Python f-string me variable).
  • Function ke parameter ka naam = braces ke andar wala naam (same hona zaroori).
  • : int = type hint. Matlab product_id hamesha integer.

Logic lagana (real filter):

python
@app.get("/product/{product_id}")
def get_one_product(product_id: int):
    one_product = None
    for p in products:
        if p.get("id") == product_id:
            one_product = p
            return one_product
    return {"error": "Product not found for this id"}
  • id 1 → mobile phone mila, id 2 → mila, id 3 → "not found".
  • Server restart karna pada, isliye --reload / fastapi dev use karo (auto refresh).

Tareeka 2: Query Parameter

Data key=value form me, URL me ? ke baad:

/greet?name=Pratik
/greet?name=Rohit&age=22
  • ? (question mark) se query params shuru, & se multiple key-value alag hote hain.
  • Google example: google.com/search?q=fastapi+documentation. q key hai, search text value. Google ise query param ki tarah receive karta hai.

Code:

python
@app.get("/greet")
def greet_user(name: str, age: int):
    return {"message": f"Hello {name}, your age is {age}"}
  • Jo parameter path me {} me nahi hai, FastAPI use automatically query param maan leta hai. Isiliye video bola "FastAPI bahut smart hai".
  • Type bhi declare karo (str, int).

Path vs Query: video ka rule

Path Param Query Param
Format /product/5 /greet?name=A&age=22
Kab Fixed, compulsory dynamic values (e.g. id + date, hamesha 2) Pata nahi kitne key-value aayenge (1, 2, n...)
Route me {} me define karna padta hai Define karne ki zarurat nahi (function args se mil jaata)

Bonus: Request object se saare query params

Jab pata na ho kitne query params aayenge:

python
from fastapi import Request

@app.get("/greet")
def greet_user(request: Request):
    query_params = dict(request.query_params)
    print(query_params)           # {'name': 'Rohit', 'age': '22'}
    return {"message": f"Hello {query_params.get('name')}, your age is {query_params.get('age')}"}
  • Har API call ek request hai. Request ke andar sab kuch: query params, body, path params, IP address...
  • FastAPI ko batana padta hai ki "mujhe request chahiye" → request: Request (type hint se).
  • request.query_params ek Pydantic-like/special object hai, dict() se normal dictionary banti hai.
  • Fayda: kal ko email bhi bhejna ho to code change kiye bina same variable me aa jaayega.
  • Ye concept har language/framework me same hai (Java, Django, Node...): sirf handle karne ka pattern thoda alag.

🧠 Insight (Video 4): yahan sabse zyada gold hai

  1. ⚠️ Correction (important!): "Path = fixed count, Query = unknown count" simplification hai. Industry ka asli rule:
    • Path param = resource ki identity (kaunsa user, kaunsa product): /users/42, /orders/991/items/3.
    • Query param = filter / sort / search / pagination / optional flags: /products?category=phone&min_price=500&sort=price&limit=20&offset=40.
    • Test: "Is value ke bina resource hi exist nahi karta?" → path. "Ye sirf list ko narrow/arrange karta hai?" → query.
  2. Declared params >> request.query_params. Video wala Request approach kaam to karta hai, lekin tum validation, type conversion, aur /docs documentation sab kho dete ho. Production me hamesha explicit declare karo:
    python
    from typing import Annotatedfrom fastapi import Query@app.get("/products")def list_products(    category: str | None = None,    min_price: Annotated[int, Query(ge=0)] = 0,    limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=100)] = 20,    offset: Annotated[int, Query(ge=0)] = 0,): ...
    Request object sirf escape hatch hai (raw headers, client IP, dynamic unknown keys).
  3. Type hints sirf documentation nahi, validation + conversion hain. /product/abc pe product_id: int hai to FastAPI khud 422 Unprocessable Entity deta hai. "22" string ko int me convert bhi karta hai (coercion). Tumhe try/except int() likhna nahi padta.
  4. Query params hamesha string aate hain (raw HTTP me). dict(request.query_params) me '22' string tha, video me bhi dikha. Isiliye declared age: int use karna safer.
  5. Optional params: name: str | None = None. Default value diya = optional. Default nahi diya = required (missing hone pe 422).
  6. Multiple values ek key ke liye: /items?tag=a&tag=b → tag: Annotated[list[str], Query()] = []. dict(request.query_params) aisa case silently last value rakhta hai (data loss bug).
  7. Path param ke liye bhi validation: Annotated[int, Path(ge=1)] → id 0 ya negative reject.
  8. Error return mat karo 200 ke saath. Video me return {"error": "..."} ka status code 200 OK hota hai: client ko lagta hai success hua. Sahi tareeka:
    python
    from fastapi import HTTPExceptionraise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Product not found")
    Frontend, monitoring tools, retries, caches: sab status codes pe depend karte hain.
  9. Linear search (for loop) = O(n). 10 products me theek hai, 10 lakh me nahi. Real me DB index (primary key lookup O(log n)) ya in-memory me dict[id] → product use karo (O(1)).
  10. Mock data ki limitations (agle video me bhi aayega): global list = per-process memory. Server restart → data gaya. Multiple workers (--workers 4) → har worker ki alag copy. Isliye mock sirf learning ke liye.
  11. Sensitive data URL me mat daalo (password, token, OTP). URLs server logs, browser history, proxies me save ho jaate hain. Sensitive cheez → header ya body.
  12. Naming convention: collection ke liye plural noun (/products), single ke liye /products/{id}. Video me /product/{id} aur /products dono use hue: kaam karta hai par consistent rakho (/products/{id}).
  13. Pagination hamesha rakho. GET /products jo sab kuch return kare, ek din 5 lakh rows ke saath server girayega. limit/offset ya cursor pagination default me daalo.

<a id="video-5"></a>

Video 5: HTTP Methods (Theory)

Client aur Server

  • Client = jise kuch chahiye (browser, mobile app, ya doosra backend server).
  • Server = jiske paas data hai aur system handle karne ki permission hai.
  • Do backend servers aapas me baat karein to ek client, ek server ban jaata hai.
  • Server khud bhi data database se maangta hai (agle videos me).

Chaar main methods

Method Kab Real-life example CRUD
GET Server se data lena Products list dekhna Read
POST Server ko naya data bhejna (store karne ke liye) Instagram pe post daalna Create
PUT Existing data update/edit karna. Data + data ki id dono bhejte hain Product ka title badalna Update
DELETE Data delete karna. Id bhejte hain Product hatana Delete

Server har request ke response me kuch return karta hai (data ya confirmation).

CRUD

Chaaron methods ka group = CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete). Almost har web application iske upar chalti hai.

Video 6 me ye bhi bola

Browser se hum sirf GET call kar sakte hain (URL bar). POST/PUT/DELETE direct browser se nahi: iske liye tools (Postman).

🧠 Insight (Video 5)

  1. Do aur methods jo jaanne zaroori hain:

    • PATCH: partial update (sirf wahi field bhejo jo badalni hai).
    • HEAD / OPTIONS: HEAD = bina body ke headers; OPTIONS = CORS preflight (browser frontend se cross-origin call karne se pehle ye bhejta hai. Isliye jab frontend alag domain pe ho to CORS middleware lagana padta hai).

  2. PUT vs PATCH:

    • PUT = poora resource replace (jo bhejoge wahi final state, baaki fields gayab/default).
    • PATCH = sirf diye hue fields badlo. Video me jo "PUT" bana wo full replace hai. Real apps me user "sirf price badlo" chahta hai → PATCH.

  3. Safe & Idempotent concept (interview + real bugs):

    Method Safe (data nahi badalta) Idempotent (N baar call = 1 baar ka effect)
    GET ✅ ✅
    PUT ❌ ✅
    DELETE ❌ ✅
    POST ❌ ❌
    PATCH ❌ ❌ (usually)

    Kyun zaroori? Network fail hota hai, client retry karta hai. POST retry = duplicate order / double payment. Isiliye payment APIs (Stripe, Razorpay) Idempotency-Key header use karti hain: same key pe doosri baar wahi result, naya charge nahi.

  4. GET se kabhi data mat badlo. Browsers prefetch karte hain, crawlers/bots links hit karte hain: GET se "delete" ya "unsubscribe" karoge to bug ya security hole.

  5. GET ki body nahi hoti (practically). Data chahiye to query/path.

  6. Method ka matlab batata hai kya ho raha hai, URL batata hai kispe. Isiliye verbs URL me mat daalo: POST /products (✅) vs /create-product (❌ non-REST). Video me create_product, update_product jaise routes hue (learning ke liye theek), real REST me:

    GET    /products          → list
POST   /products          → create
GET    /products/{id}     → read one
PUT    /products/{id}     → full update
PATCH  /products/{id}     → partial update
DELETE /products/{id}     → delete

  7. Sahi status codes:

    Situation Code
    Read/update OK 200
    Created 201
    Delete OK, body nahi 204
    Client ki galti (bad input) 400 / 422 (FastAPI validation)
    Login nahi 401
    Permission nahi 403
    Nahi mila 404
    Duplicate / conflict 409
    Server crash 500

  8. CRUD ke aage: real systems me sab kuch CRUD nahi hota (e.g. "checkout", "cancel order", "send OTP"). Aise actions ke liye POST /orders/{id}/cancel jaise sub-resource routes common hain.

<a id="video-6"></a>

Video 6: POST, PUT, DELETE + Pydantic (DTO / Validation)

Aaj ke 3 topics

  1. Different HTTP methods ke routes kaise banaye
  2. Data validation kaise karein
  3. In methods ko kaise call/test karein (tool)

1) POST route banana

python
@app.post("/create-product")
def create_product():
    return {"status": "Product created successfully"}

Bas get ki jagah post. Baaki sab same.

2) Browser limitation

Browser URL bar se sirf GET. POST/PUT/DELETE test karne ke liye client tool: Postman.

Postman ka basic structure

  • Workspace: alag projects / clients ke liye alag space (internal, team ke saath share kar sakte ho).
  • Collection: ek workspace ke andar alag systems (User, Product, Orders, Cart) ki requests ka group.
  • Request: ek API call: method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS) + URL.
  • Save: Ctrl + S. Red dot = unsaved.

Naming standard: request ko clear naam do (Get One Product, Create New Product) taaki dekhte hi pata chale kya karta hai. Company standards me ye important hai.

Data bhejne ke 3 tareeke (kisi bhi method ke saath)

  1. Body: POST/PUT ke saath (mostly)
  2. Headers: request headers (auth tokens etc., aage cover hoga)
  3. Query params

POST me body bhejna zaroori nahi ki sirf body hi ho; teeno bheje ja sakte hain.

Postman me body

Body → raw → JSON. JSON = key-value pairs (dictionary/object).

json
{
  "id": 3,
  "title": "Mens Watch",
  "price": 2500,
  "count": 45
}

Backend me body receive karna: Pydantic

Sirf variable ka naam body rakhne se body nahi aati. Iske liye Pydantic:

  • Python ke liye data types / validation library.
  • FastAPI install karte time saath me hi install ho gayi.
  • Docs: FastAPI → Learn → Tutorial → Request Body.
    • Request body = client → API ko bheja data. Response body = API → client ko bheja data.

DTO banana (dtos.py)

DTO = Data Transfer Object (isse "data validation schema" bhi bol sakte ho).

python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class ProductDTO(BaseModel):
    id: int
    title: str
    price: int = 0
    count: int = 0
  • Class ko BaseModel se inherit karte hain (OOP inheritance) taaki Pydantic ki saari powers mil jaayein.
  • Jo field required hai (bina default) wo bhejna padega.
  • Default value (= 0) wala field optional ban jaata hai.
  • (Aage: Optional, multiple types: str | int, etc.)

Route me DTO use karna

python
from dtos import ProductDTO

@app.post("/create-product")
def create_product(product_data: ProductDTO):
    print(product_data)
    return {"status": "Product created successfully"}

Ab jo body aayegi wo product_data me milegi, validated.

Validation ke 2 demo

Case Result
title nahi bheja 422 Unprocessable Content, detail me loc: body → title, msg: Field required
count nahi bheja Error nahi, count 0 default se store hota hai

Pydantic object → dictionary

python
product_data = product_data.model_dump()

model_dump() Pydantic object ko normal dict me badalta hai.

Data store karna (mock memory me)

python
products.append(product_data)
return products

Naya product add hua, wapas list me dikhta bhi hai. GET /product/3, /product/4 ab data dete hain, /product/5 pe "not found".

PUT route (update)

python
@app.put("/update-product/{product_id}")
def update_product(product_id: int, product_data: ProductDTO):
    for index, one_product in enumerate(products):
        if one_product.get("id") == product_id:
            products[index] = product_data.model_dump()
            return {"status": "Product updated successfully", "product": products[index]}
    return {"error": "Product not found with this id"}

Logic samjho:

  • Update ke liye do cheezein chahiye: data (body) + id (path param).
  • Mock data list hai to hume index chahiye (kis position pe replace karna hai). enumerate() index + item dono deta hai.
  • Id match → us index pe naya data replace → updated product return (taaki client ko pata chale kya update hua).
  • Match nahi → "not found".

Video ka debugging lesson 🐞

Pehle products[index] = product_data (seedha Pydantic object) store kiya → GET by id pe error (internal server error). Reason: list ke andar ab dictionary nahi, Pydantic object tha. one_product.get("id") object pe nahi chalta. Fix: product_data.model_dump() (dict banake store karo).

DELETE route

python
@app.delete("/delete-product/{product_id}")
def delete_product(product_id: int):
    for index, one_product in enumerate(products):
        if one_product.get("id") == product_id:
            deleted_product = products.pop(index)
            return {"status": "Product deleted successfully", "product": deleted_product}
    return {"error": "Product not found with this id"}
  • Body nahi chahiye, sirf id.
  • Id aur index alag hote hain (id 2 ho sakti hai, index 0 ho sakta hai) kyunki data manual hai, DB nahi.
  • list.pop(index) index pe se item hata ke return karta hai.
  • Test: DELETE /delete-product/2 → deleted. Phir GET /product/2 → not found. ✅

Result: CRUD complete ✅

Create (POST) ✔ Read (GET all + GET one) ✔ Update (PUT) ✔ Delete (DELETE) ✔

🧠 Insight (Video 6): sabse important section

1) Client ko ID kabhi mat dene do (create me)

Video me body me "id": 3 client bhej raha hai. Real me id server/DB generate karta hai (auto-increment / UUID). Warna:

  • Client duplicate id bhej dega (id 3 do baar) → data corrupt.
  • Koi jaanbujhkar kisi aur ki id bhej ke overwrite karne ki koshish karega. Isliye Create schema me id hoti hi nahi.

2) Ek hi DTO sabke liye = anti-pattern. 3-4 schemas rakho

ProductCreate  → client jo bhejta hai (id nahi)
ProductUpdate  → PUT ke liye (full)
ProductPatch   → sab fields Optional (PATCH ke liye)
ProductOut     → client ko jo wapas jaata hai (id + safe fields)

Ye Mass Assignment vulnerability rokta hai (jaise client is_admin: true bhej de aur tumhara code seedha save kar de). Output schema me password hash, internal fields kabhi nahi jaane chahiye: response_model=ProductOut ye enforce karta hai.

3) Pydantic ki asli powers (abhi sirf type check dekha)

python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class ProductCreate(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    price: int = Field(ge=0)
    count: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)
  • ge/le/gt/lt, min_length/max_length, pattern (regex)
  • EmailStr, HttpUrl, datetime, UUID, Enum, Literal["a","b"]
  • @field_validator, @model_validator (custom rules)
  • Coercion: "5" → 5 (default "lax mode"). Strict chahiye to strict=True.
  • Extra fields: Pydantic default me extra keys ignore karta hai. Reject karna ho: model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid").

4) price ko int rakhna sahi hai, paise me

Paisa kabhi float me store mat karo (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3). Ya to paise (integer minor units) me (₹25.00 = 2500 paise) ya Decimal. Ye har fintech/e-commerce engineer ka pehla paath hai.

5) Update ka "mutable list" logic fragile hai

  • Global list thread-safe nahi (race conditions).
  • Multiple workers = alag copy, data inconsistent.
  • Restart = data gaya.
  • Iterate-karte-time-modify safe sirf isliye tha kyunki turant return kiya. Real me: DB + transactions. Mock ke liye bhi dict[int, dict] use karo to loops hat jaate hain (O(1)).

6) PUT replace hota hai: exclude_unset se PATCH

python
# PATCH logic
changes = patch_data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)   # sirf wahi jo client ne bheja
stored.update(changes)

exclude_unset=True = "jo field client ne bheji hi nahi use mat chhedo" (default values se overwrite na ho). Ye subtle bug hai: bina iske count default 0 se overwrite ho jaata.

7) Duplicate create rokna → 409 Conflict

Video me same id do baar POST ho sakti hai. Check karo aur 409 do. DB me unique constraint lagao (app-level check race condition me fail hota hai; DB constraint final authority hai).

8) Status codes sahi do

POST → 201 Created, DELETE → 204 No Content, not found → HTTPException(404). Video me sab 200 + {"error": ...} hai: learning ke liye ok, production ke liye galat.

9) 422 error format = free gift

FastAPI/Pydantic ka error response (loc, msg, type) already structured hai: frontend isse field-wise errors dikha sakta hai. Ise consume karna seekho. Custom error format chahiye to exception_handler likho aur poori API me ek consistent error shape rakho (e.g. RFC 9457 "Problem Details").

10) print() → logging

Video me print(product_data) debugging ke liye. Production me logging (levels, timestamps, structured JSON logs). Request body me sensitive data (password, card) kabhi log mat karo.

11) Testing: Postman ke alawa

  • /docs (Swagger UI): built-in, zero setup.
  • curl: curl -X POST localhost:8000/products -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title":"Watch","price":2500}'
  • Automated tests (asli skill):
    python
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClientclient = TestClient(app)def test_create_product():    r = client.post("/products", json={"title": "Watch", "price": 2500})    assert r.status_code == 201
    Postman manual testing hai; pytest + TestClient regression se bachata hai. Senior engineer ka "kaam ho gaya" = tests pass.

12) Postman best practices (video ne jo kaha uska extension)

  • Base URL ko environment variable banao ({{base_url}}): local/staging/prod switch ek click me.
  • Collection ko team ke saath share/export karo (docs ka kaam bhi karta hai).
  • OpenAPI schema (/openapi.json) Postman me import ho sakta hai: saari requests auto-ban jaati hain.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from mock_data import products
from dtos import ProductDTO

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def home():
    return "Welcome to FastAPI series"

@app.get("/products")
def get_products():
    return products

@app.get("/product/{product_id}")
def get_one_product(product_id: int):
    for p in products:
        if p.get("id") == product_id:
            return p
    return {"error": "Product not found for this id"}

@app.get("/greet")
def greet_user(request: Request):
    q = dict(request.query_params)
    return {"message": f"Hello {q.get('name')}, your age is {q.get('age')}"}

@app.post("/create-product")
def create_product(product_data: ProductDTO):
    products.append(product_data.model_dump())
    return products

@app.put("/update-product/{product_id}")
def update_product(product_id: int, product_data: ProductDTO):
    for index, p in enumerate(products):
        if p.get("id") == product_id:
            products[index] = product_data.model_dump()
            return {"status": "Product updated successfully", "product": products[index]}
    return {"error": "Product not found with this id"}

@app.delete("/delete-product/{product_id}")
def delete_product(product_id: int):
    for index, p in enumerate(products):
        if p.get("id") == product_id:
            deleted = products.pop(index)
            return {"status": "Product deleted successfully", "product": deleted}
    return {"error": "Product not found with this id"}

<a id="production-version"></a>

Production-grade version (wahi API, senior tareeke se)

Video wale code ko in sudhaaron ke saath dekho: har badlav ka reason upar insights me hai.

python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Path, Query, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

app = FastAPI(title="Products API", version="1.0.0")


# ---------- Schemas (DTOs) ----------
class ProductBase(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")      # unknown fields reject
    title: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)
    price: int = Field(ge=0, description="Price in paise")
    count: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)


class ProductCreate(ProductBase):
    """Client create ke time id nahi bhejta."""


class ProductReplace(ProductBase):
    """PUT: poora replace."""


class ProductPatch(BaseModel):
    """PATCH: sab optional."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    title: str | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=100)
    price: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    count: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)


class ProductOut(ProductBase):
    id: int


# ---------- In-memory "DB" (sirf learning ke liye) ----------
db: dict[int, dict] = {
    1: {"id": 1, "title": "mobile phone", "price": 100000, "count": 10},
    2: {"id": 2, "title": "Apple MacBook", "price": 1000000, "count": 12},
}
_next_id = 3

ProductId = Annotated[int, Path(ge=1)]


def _get_or_404(product_id: int) -> dict:
    product = db.get(product_id)
    if product is None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, "Product not found")
    return product


# ---------- Routes ----------
@app.get("/products", response_model=list[ProductOut])
def list_products(
    search: str | None = None,
    min_count: Annotated[int, Query(ge=0)] = 0,
    limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=100)] = 20,
    offset: Annotated[int, Query(ge=0)] = 0,
):
    items = list(db.values())
    if search:
        items = [p for p in items if search.lower() in p["title"].lower()]
    items = [p for p in items if p["count"] >= min_count]
    return items[offset : offset + limit]


@app.get("/products/{product_id}", response_model=ProductOut)
def get_product(product_id: ProductId):
    return _get_or_404(product_id)


@app.post("/products", response_model=ProductOut, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
def create_product(data: ProductCreate):
    global _next_id
    product = {"id": _next_id, **data.model_dump()}
    db[_next_id] = product
    _next_id += 1
    return product


@app.put("/products/{product_id}", response_model=ProductOut)
def replace_product(product_id: ProductId, data: ProductReplace):
    _get_or_404(product_id)
    db[product_id] = {"id": product_id, **data.model_dump()}
    return db[product_id]


@app.patch("/products/{product_id}", response_model=ProductOut)
def patch_product(product_id: ProductId, data: ProductPatch):
    product = _get_or_404(product_id)
    product.update(data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True))
    return product


@app.delete("/products/{product_id}", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
def delete_product(product_id: ProductId):
    _get_or_404(product_id)
    del db[product_id]

<a id="assumptions"></a>

Assumptions / Doubts: sab solve

Q1. "Fast hai" matlab main Express/Node se tez hu? Nahi guaranteed. Python frameworks me FastAPI top pe hai; Node (Express/Fastify) comparable ya zyada fast ho sakta hai. Asli performance DB, caching, architecture se aati hai.

Q2. Path param sirf tab jab ek hi value ho? Nahi. Video ne khud correct kiya. Rule: path = resource identity, query = filter/sort/optional. Path me multiple bhi ho sakte hain (/users/5/orders/9).

Q3. POST me sirf body hoti hai? Nahi. Body + headers + query: teeno ho sakte hain. Convention me create data body me jaata hai.

Q4. Browser se POST/PUT/DELETE kyun nahi? URL bar sirf GET karta hai. JavaScript (fetch/axios) se browser sab methods bhej sakta hai. Limitation address bar ki hai, browser ki nahi. Frontend app ke liye CORS settings chahiye.

Q5. fastapi dev main.py aur uvicorn main:app --reload me fark? Dono same kaam (auto-reload dev server). fastapi dev newer CLI wrapper hai (uvicorn upar chalta hai). Production: fastapi run ya uvicorn --workers N (reload nahi).

Q6. main:app me main aur app kya? main = file ka naam (main.py), app = us file ke andar FastAPI() ka variable. Variable ka naam app zaroori nahi, bas command me wahi likho.

Q7. Pydantic object aur dict me kya fark? Object = typed, validated, attributes (data.title). Dict = plain key-value (d["title"]). .model_dump() object → dict, Model(**d) dict → object. List me Pydantic object daala to .get("id") fail hoga (video ka bug).

Q8. Pydantic v1 vs v2? Tutorial me model_dump() = v2 syntax. Purane tutorials me .dict() (v1) milega. v2 me .dict() deprecated hai, hamesha model_dump() use karo.

Q9. 422 aur 400 me kya fark? 400 = generic bad request. 422 = request syntax theek hai (valid JSON) par semantic/validation fail (field missing, wrong type). FastAPI validation errors ke liye 422 deta hai.

Q10. Mock data kab tak? Sirf prototype/learning ke liye. Persistent storage (DB) next step hai (SQL series me aa raha).

Q11. Mere route kaam kyun nahi kar raha (video ki 2 galtiyan)?

  1. Decorator (@app.get(...)) lagana bhool gaye → function sirf normal function hai → 404.
  2. Server restart nahi hua (reload off) → purana code chal raha hai. Checklist: decorator? path sahi? method sahi? param naam path ke {} se match? server reload hua? /docs me route dikh raha hai?

Q12. Request body vs Response body? Request body = client → server. Response body = server → client. Dono ke liye alag schema rakho (ProductCreate vs ProductOut).

<a id="cheatsheet"></a>

10-saal-wale lessons: cheat sheet

API design

  1. URLs = nouns, methods = verbs. POST /orders, na ki /createOrder.
  2. Consistent naming: plural, lowercase, hyphen (/product-categories).
  3. Versioning shuru se: /api/v1/.... Breaking change aaye to /v2.
  4. Pagination + filtering + sorting list endpoints me default.
  5. Consistent error shape poori API me.
  6. Idempotency: payment/order jaise POST ke liye Idempotency-Key.
  7. Kabhi breaking change silently mat karo: field hatana/rename = client crash.

Validation & security

  1. Client pe kabhi bharosa nahi. Har input validate: type, range, length, enum.
  2. Server-generated: id, timestamps, user_id (token se), role: client se kabhi mat lo.
  3. Output schema se sensitive fields filter (response_model).
  4. Secrets .env me, git me nahi. pydantic-settings se typed config.
  5. CORS sirf trusted origins ke liye (* production me nahi).
  6. Rate limiting (login, OTP, public endpoints).
  7. SQL injection: ORM / parameterized queries; raw string concatenation kabhi nahi.

Reliability & performance

  1. Blocking call async def me mat daalo.
  2. N+1 queries (loop me DB call) sabse common performance killer.
  3. Index woh columns pe jo WHERE/JOIN/ORDER BY me aate hain.
  4. Slow kaam background me (email, PDF, report): BackgroundTasks chhote kaam ke liye, Celery/RQ/RabbitMQ reliable queues ke liye (retries, persistence).
  5. Timeouts: har outgoing HTTP/DB call pe timeout. Bina timeout ke ek slow dependency poora server rok deti hai.
  6. Health check endpoint: GET /health (deployment/Kubernetes ke liye).

Code quality

  1. Layers: routers → services (business logic) → repositories (DB). Route handler patla rakho.
  2. Tests likho (pytest + TestClient). Bug fix pe pehle failing test, phir fix.
  3. Type hints har jagah: IDE + mypy/pyright bugs pehle pakadte hain.
  4. Logging (structured), print nahi. Request-id har log me.
  5. Dependency pinning (lockfile). "Latest" install = random breakage.
  6. 12-factor config: code same, config environment se.
  7. Docs ko code ke saath rakho: FastAPI /docs free deta hai: summary, description, tags, response_model, examples bharo.

Mindset

  1. Pehle chalao, phir sahi karo, phir tez karo, par "sahi" (validation, status codes, tests) ko "tez" se pehle rakho.
  2. Boring technology jeet-ti hai: Postgres + simple queries 90% apps ke liye kaafi.
  3. Debug karna = padhna: error message poora padho (Video 6 me bug ka answer error ke andar hi tha: 'ProductDTO' object has no attribute 'get' type message).
